label: <DEL> delimiter step (sequences of length >= 5)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively on the <DEL> delimiter input (98.6% of activation mass; the top activations are all at <DEL>, near the max of 0.55). It fires on about 72% of delimiter steps: never when L=3, rarely when L=4 (3% of activations, weak), and on roughly 80-90% of delimiters when L>=5. Magnitude does not track L monotonically. A small residue (1.4% of mass) is weak firing on late original-phase tokens (orig_idx 5-8) in long sequences, usually the step just before <DEL>. It never fires during the copy phase. Some L>=5 delimiters stay silent; excluding particular first tokens or a digit at position 3 did not help. Which original tokens appear changes the activation only a little (lift about 1.2-1.3x for first tokens w/j/n).

issues: Overstatement: the explanation says the feature fires 'rarely and weakly when L=4'. In fact it fires on 25.6% of L=4 delimiter steps (dev precision 0.256, test 0.257), and those steps hold 3.4% of the mass. That is a minority of steps, but not rare.

Precision at the delimiter is not flat across L>=5: 0.81 (L=5), 0.92 (L=6), 0.90 (L=7), 0.81 (L=8), 0.70 (L=9). The firing rate falls off at L=9. The label does not mention this, but it is a graded decline, not a clean exclusion.

The last original token (prev_tok) shifts the firing rate in a diffuse way: delimiter precision runs from 0.61 (prev=i) to 0.98 (prev=q/0). Excluding the low-precision tokens lowered test F1 (0.817 vs 0.874), so this is graded modulation, not a separable class.

Claims I verified: zero activity in the copy phase; zero at L=3; 98.6% of mass on <DEL>; an original-phase residue of 1.4% only at orig_idx 5-8; top activations all on <DEL>; test P/R/F1 = 0.827/0.928/0.874, mass recall 0.952. Digit content (n_digits, a '3' in the sequence) does not change delimiter precision (about 0.78-0.86 throughout).
